title: I-Kaz methodology for predicting tool life of AlCrN—Coated WC—Co inserts in the machining of AISI 304 steel
author: Chinnasamy, Rathanasamy, et al.

steps.title: Prepare cutting inserts
steps.instruction: Obtain uncoated carbide inserts (model XDHT090308‑THM) from Widia Pvt. Ltd. and deposit an AlCrN coating on them using physical vapour deposition on the Oerlikon Balzer industrial coating system.

steps.title: Prepare AISI 304 workpiece
steps.instruction: Cut stainless‑steel (AISI 304) bar to a length of 180 mm and a diameter of 70 mm. No further treatment is required.

steps.title: Configure CNC machine
steps.instruction: Power on the CNC l‑Mill 55 (maximum 6000 rpm, 11 kW). Install an M680 tool holder, mount the prepared insert (coated or uncoated), and ensure the machining is performed in a dry environment (no coolant).

steps.title: Create Taguchi L18 matrix
steps.instruction: Define three levels for each cutting parameter: spindle speed – 750, 1000, 1250 rpm; feed rate – 0.02, 0.04, 0.06 mm/rev; depth of cut – 0.5, 0.75, 1 mm. Use these levels to generate an L18 orthogonal array according to Taguchi design of experiments.

steps.title: Execute milling experiment
steps.instruction: For each trial in the L18 array, set the spindle speed, feed rate, and depth of cut as specified, run the machining for exactly 10 minutes, and acquire acoustic data continuously with a Microflown sensor linked to a high‑precision data acquisition system. Use LabVIEW to record sound pressure and velocity signals, generating a total of 70 000 cycles; calculate the I‑Kaz coefficient Z₂α every 10 000‑cycle interval.

steps.title: Measure flank wear
steps.instruction: After each 10‑minute run, inspect the insert flank and measure the wear width VB (e.g., ~0.011 mm at 10 000 cycles, ~0.028 mm at 70 000 cycles) with appropriate metrology equipment.

steps.title: Analyze I‑Kaz relationship
steps.instruction: Plot the measured Z₂α values against the corresponding VB values and fit the data to the power‑law model Z₂α = a·VB^(‑n) to obtain constants a and n for the given cutting parameters.

steps.title: Run real‑time wear GUI
steps.instruction: Load the optimized cutting parameters into the provided GUI application, monitor the sound‑pressure signal in real time, and display the predicted flank wear based on the calculated I‑Kaz coefficient.
